BasePK: 2959829
Chunk index: 0

Speech chunk:
The minister mentioned the National Energy Board Act on which, obviously, many of his legal conclusions are based. Did that act not make clear the constitutional right of producing provinces to fix the wellhead price? Conflicting claims about the right to fix prices have arisen in Canada from time to time. Some contend that the provinces alone have the right to fix the wellhead price, and some contend that the federal government, by virtue of the National Energy Board Act, is given certain rights in this regard. For instance, the federal government has authority over the transport and/or export of natural gas and oil and petroleum products and, by that means, can indirectly fix prices. The federal government has always had that right. It has always exercised authority with regard to price fixing. The Diefenbaker government recognized the situation and provided for provincial rights to be left with the provinces.

During International Women's Year a number of women's associations drew the attention of Canadians and of people elsewhere in the world to the existence of certain women political prisoners in the U.S.S.R.
